author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has threatened to attack US military bases across the Middle East if American warships continue escorting vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC says it attacked four ships in the northern Gulf over alleged illegal oil transfers, while three others reportedly struck mines in the strait. Neither claim has been independently verified. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says at least 14 vessels were attacked between October 8 and 17, with shipping traffic remaining 70 percent below pre-war levels. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump claims oil shipments through Hormuz have exceeded pre-war levels and that Washington has complete control of the waterway, despite figures showing a sharp decline in vessel crossings. Trump blames Iran for shipping disruptions as rising fuel, food and household costs fuel voter frustration ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections. 

Al Jazeera's Mohammad Vall reports from Tehran, and Kimberly H
title: Iran threatens US bases as Trump claims Hormuz oil shipments exceed pre-war levels

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Hope Hooton and Kellie Elliott feared their children were not safe with their fathers. Hope sought protection after her husband threatened suicide and later experienced a psychiatric crisis. Kellie documented years of domestic violence and abuse. Yet both fathers had unsupervised time with their children, whom they later killed.

Through the stories of these two mothers, Fault Lines investigates how evidence of danger can be missed, dismissed or fail to reach family courts at all. The film examines the push for equal custody, the failure to treat violence against a parent as a risk to children and the changes advocates say could prevent other families from suffering the same losses.

Director & Producer: Amina Waheed
Correspondent: Natasha Del Toro
Director of Photography: Joel Van Haren
Editor: Adrienne Haspel
Executive Producer: Laila Al-Arian
Associate Producer & Fact Checking: Mehr Sher
Additional field production: Nicolas Pollack and Jeremy Young
Production Management: Anabelle R
title: Fatal Custody: How family courts missed domestic violence warning signs | Fault Lines

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United States ambassador to Turkiye and special presidential envoy for Syria and Iraq says Washington’s relationship with the countries in the Middle East needs to change.

Tom Barrack says the US no longer seeks to dominate the region.

He won’t say whether the war in Iran was a mistake – but acknowledges the instability it caused has led to unintended consequences.

Barrack says President Donald Trump is against what he calls "forever wars", and ending the US-Israel war on Iran will require a major compromise. According to him, each side will have to accept conditions it does not like.

However, he is worried that growing tensions could lead to miscalculation.

Barrack says trust is lacking between Washington and Tehran, and that is hampering talks to agree on a deal.

He tells Al Jazeera that countries in the region should not depend on the US to solve their problems and that they need to look out for themselves. He insists the Trump administration has not abandoned the region,
title: US Ambassador to Turkiye: Iran war’s unintended consequences | Talk to Al Jazeera

description:
More than 400 people, mostly children, have fallen ill after E. coli contaminated the water supply in Tshwane, South Africa. The crisis was linked to a lack of chlorine at a water treatment plant, leaving residents concerned about the safety of their tap water.
Residents describe dirty water and the struggle to find safe alternatives for drinking and cooking. The government has procured chlorine and promised water tankers, but many families say they cannot afford to buy bottled water as they wait for a reliable supply.
Al Jazeera's Clement Manyathela reports from Tshwane, South Africa.

Protests in France have highlighted growing anger over police tactics and deteriorating university conditions. Landry Ngang, deputy mayor of Saint-Denis, near Paris, says he was tear-gassed by police while attempting to de-escalate a street situation. Meanwhile, students at Paris 8 University are protesting over deteriorating campus facilities, a lack of teachers and inadequate public funding. Many say the situation has left them disillusioned about their future prospects in France.
